messages:
ashok: Heads up — SFO GPU pool dropped to ~35% available at 14:02 UTC, several low-priority hosted routes saw throttling. autoscaler logs showing failed launches.
oncall-bot: [14:02] alert: gpu_pool_utilization_high (sfo-gpu-pool) severity=warning
maria: copying logs, grabbing `kubectl get pods -n infra -o wide` now
ryan: I can see OOM eviction and instance launch failures 13:58-14:04, error: API quota exceeded for region-sfo.
jenna: region quotas? Did we hit cloud provider vCPU/GPU soft limits?
maria: provider message: "Quota limit for NVIDIAGPUs reached for region SFO-1" — created support ticket 123456.
ashok: (typo) sorry, ashok here — yes support ticket raised, but we need runbook actions to restore capacity and route traffic.
ryan: immediate mitigations: 1) shift low-priority traffic to AMS and LAX by weight-slice, 2) enable reserved-burst on dedicated pools, 3) drain noncritical jobs.
jenna: I can push a weighted shift using the routing api. Proposed weights: SFO 0.5 -> 0.2 for hosted dev-tier, shift 30% to AMS, 20% to LAX. Any objections?
maria: +1. Also suggest relaxing prefix caching window for a minute to reduce tokens going to backend.
ashok: Go ahead on routing change. Ryan, can you kick autoscaler debug: `infra/scale-debug.sh --pool sfo-gpu-pool --verbose` and paste stack traces?
ryan: running it now, output shows GCE API 429 errors and transient network timeouts to control-plane. Posting snippet: ```ERROR: gcp: quotaExceeded: requested 4 GPUs, available 0; retry after 30s
Traceback (most recent call last): ...```.
jenna: routing change done: `POST /routing/v1/weights` payload: `{dev:{sfo:0.2,ams:0.5,lax:0.3}}`. Observability: latency for dev-tier back to baseline within 45s. :thumbsup:
maria: started draining noncritical batch jobs: `k get pods -l job=batch -n workloads` then `kubectl cordon/evict`. Evictions reduced pending queue by ~12.
ryan: confirming autoscaler still hitting API quota; cloud support says slow lift — estimate 30-90 mins. We should rely on cross-region shift and dedicated reserved bursts until quota clears.
ashok: Noted cost impact — shifting to AMS/LAX increases egress between regions for some customers. Please make a quick cost note and tag finance.
jenna: FYI I updated the incident channel with a short status: "SFO GPU quota hit, traffic shifted to AMS/LAX, reserved-burst enabled, support ticket 123456."
oncall-bot: [14:18] status:update incident-1785503210 severity=warning state=mitigated
maria: Postmortem / runbook improvements I propose: 1) add preflight quota check to autoscaler (fail open to routing when quota errors persist), 2) add automated weighted-slice routine for sudden pool drops, 3) maintain a soft spare GPU reservation to avoid immediate customer impact, 4) document cost/egress tradeoffs for cross-region shifts.
ryan: +1. Also suggest a health-check circuit in the control-plane: if the pool is below X% for >Y seconds and autoscaler sees API 429s, flip to traffic-slice mode and notify finance/sales for customers in impacted regions.
jenna: I'll open a PR to `infra/runbooks/region-failover.md` with the weighted-slice play and the `scale-debug.sh` steps. Assigning reviewers: @ryan @maria.
ashok: Action items from thread: - jenna: PR to runbook with weighted-slice and communication steps (due EOD) - ryan: add autoscaler preflight to detect quota 429 and fallback routing logic (RFC by EOW) - maria: add automation to drain noncritical batch jobs on low-pool signal (prototype next week) - jenna: notify finance for cost delta estimate (cc: @finance)
jenna: I'll also add a step to the runbook to flip on reserved-burst for Dedicated pools and to annotate what % reserved should be held (proposal: 5% soft reserve).
maria: final note — once quota lifts, we should do a controlled rebalance: gradual weight restoration over 10 minutes, and run smoke tests for latency and token cost.
ashok: Thanks team. Keeping this thread open for follow-ups. Will post postmortem once we have root cause and timeline.
oncall-bot: [14:35] resolved alert: gpu_pool_utilization_high (sfo-gpu-pool) severity=info
